review.verdict: LENS C1, prospective call/lock design: REVISION REQUIRED as a design. Nothing was run, and this verdict gives no source permission. The protocol core is COMPATIBLE AS DESIGN with doc 49's 5C held design (f1821b6:50,56), the 462cf79 correction, doc 51 and the 7b1e606 carry-forwards, Samuel's scope 1d4f2c3:96-120,170-197, the currentness contract at S 25858ad and the accepted 3e82154 intake. That core is: an actor/key lock, then replay inside the transaction; preflight row locks, then the head FOR SHARE last; an AFTER-statement guard that advances the epoch only when a projection changes; a single-owner SECURITY DEFINER commit; five atomic writes and no legacy submit; persisted:true only after commit; recovery that runs before any mutable gate; readback guarded by read_all; referral kept as declarations. Three P2 gaps must close before any commit or guard body is drafted. (1) The commit's current-authority read and activation interface is unnamed. At S, read_current_authority always returns unavailable, and same-epoch owner DML can set the head state (HI-3, item 15). (2) The guard's definer/owner model is missing from the same-OID set. (3) The packet says an exact ordered lock/call/privilege specification is in its JSON, but the JSON has none. There are also eight P3 precision items. Samuel decides the operating budgets, the writer lock_timeout, the refusal budget, the first-lock-wins revocation order and the stock predicate; everything else is engineering.

checklist.item: Hand-sim 1: two concurrent submissions with the same idempotency key
checklist.evidence: Both requests find nothing on getExisting (handler.mjs:142; intake.sql:297-299) and both reach commit. The actor/key lock comes first (1d4f2c3:100; 06:15-17). T1 writes the five rows and commits. T2 then re-reads in a fresh READ COMMITTED statement: same payload gives a stored-receipt replay (200, :165); a different payload gives a conflict with no writes (06:39-40). One outbox row. If T2's lock wait exceeds lock_timeout: 55P03 → 503 → client retries the same key → replay. While unknown, the client ignores 409 catalog_changed (QuickOrderPage:141), so it never shows a false 'not accepted'. Requires the lock before every source lock (F3). NOT RUN.

checklist.item: Hand-sim 2: submission racing publish_revision (head re-held, epoch advanced)
checklist.evidence: The intake records E0 before preflight (1d4f2c3:172-178). (a) Publish commits first: the intake's head share then reads E0+1 and 'held' (currentness.sql:524-526), so it refuses and rolls back with no retry. (b) Intake holds the share first: publish waits at :507, the request commits under R0, then the head is re-held. This is first lock wins (1d4f2c3:186-188), which is reserved to Samuel. (c) Publish holds FOR UPDATE uncommitted: the intake times out, or re-reads the new head version and refuses. No partial or duplicate writes in any branch. At S nothing ever makes the head active, so every intake refuses; the success-path read is unspecified (F1).

checklist.item: Hand-sim 3: lost response, then recovery

On retry, replay runs before any gate (:140-147), admin_detail checks integrity, and the same reference returns with 200. No commit call, so no second obligation. If the original is still in flight, the retry waits on the actor/key lock and then replays. Replay ignores currentness, so recovery survives a re-held head. NOT RUN.

If W holds the head mid-transaction, the intake waits; on a cycle, lock_timeout refuses (item 23). Expiry of effectivity involves no write, so a database-time recheck after waits is needed (06:37-38). This is safe only if the actual readers match the projections; 17 rows are UNPOPULATED (JSON:311-316). See F9. NOT PROVEN.

findings.claim: The commit's current-authority read and its dependency on activation are unspecified. At S the designated reader always returns 'unavailable', and the head state alone can be set by same-epoch owner DML.
findings.evidence: currentness.sql:524-527@25858ad: publish always sets held and adds 1 to the epoch. :550-555: read_current_authority is constant 'unavailable', independent of row state. :388-390: equal epochs are allowed. Doc50:82 HI-3: same-epoch DML can rewrite state, 'mitigated by the constant reader'; future protocol must strictly increase the epoch (7b1e606:39, item 15). 1d4f2c3:146 makes the private reader the authority; :189-193,275 make activation a separate slice. JSON:1260-1269@d007162 lists currentness_integrity() but no authority reader, and md:140 gives no epoch comparison source. The body would either never pass 'held' or trust a head.state that DML can forge. Where readerCensusSha256 is compared at runtime is also unnamed (7b1e606:27).
findings.fix: Specify the commit's authority read: head FOR SHARE taken last, then one call to read_current_authority() (or a single named successor) in a fresh statement. Refuse unless it returns a closed {state:'active', revisionId, writerEpoch} equal to the E0/R0 recorded before preflight. The separate activation slice (Samuel, class 5) must replace the reader with one that requires a strict epoch increase. Compare readerCensusSha256 at activation, outside any measured reader. Until then the commit stays fail-closed.

findings.claim: The source-write guard's effective role is unspecified and missing from the same-OID precondition. As an invoker function it cannot lock or advance the head for any writer not running as the head owner.
findings.evidence: JSON:1250@d007162: the guard takes the head when a projection changes. JSON:1284's same-OID list ('fences/head/revisions/intake/commit') and 7b1e606:31 (item 11) both omit the guard. currentness.sql:374-375@25858ad revokes head and revisions from public, anon, authenticated and service_role. :482-494 refuses any grantee other than the owner, and FOR UPDATE/UPDATE on the head needs UPDATE privilege. Writers run as their RPC owner or caller (hosted owners NOT PROVEN). 06 design:42-47 says writers are never refused merely because intake is held. The currentness triggers are ENABLE ALWAYS (:405-410); the guard's enable mode is unstated.
findings.fix: Specify guard_source_write as SECURITY DEFINER, owned by the common OID, proconfig search_path='', no EXECUTE grants, its own fingerprint and ACL check, an explicit enable mode (ALWAYS like :405-410, or a justified ORIGIN), and absent/held-head behaviour per 06:42. Add the guard to the item-11 precheck, postcheck and runtime set.

findings.claim: Decision B makes an exact ordered lock/call/privilege design a precondition, but the packet does not contain it. Md:144 says it is 'specified in JSON'; the JSON holds only generic requirement lists.
findings.evidence: md:71,144@d007162 versus JSON:1260-1269 (8 generic calls, 'applicable transitives') and :1276-1288 (rules only). :1301-1306 still lists 'Prospective calls/locks/privileges' as an open gate. Census JSON:337-352,389-394,410-415 marks all five positive-lock relations UNPOPULATED. The controlling order exists only as prose (f1821b6:56; 1d4f2c3:170-185; 06:15-26). No sort key, lock mode, post-wait predicate or writer counterpart is given for members, customers, legal bindings with aliases, acceptances, the founder checkout or lot witnesses.
findings.fix: Add one ordered table to the JSON. Columns: step, object (advisory key or relation+selector), mode, sort key, NOT FOUND/ambiguity refusal, post-wait recheck using database time, writer counterpart and its order, justified 'none' rows (item 8). Order: READ COMMITTED check; actor/key lock on the 1d4f2c3:96-97 hash; replay; record E0/R0; members, customers, bindings, acceptances, checkout; lot witnesses by UUID; session; head FOR SHARE; fresh reads; inserts. Correct md:144.

findings.claim: A witness-lot intake that waits on lot locks can deadlock with an unreplaced multi-SKU FEFO reserve, and the deadlock detector may abort the customer reservation instead of the intake.
findings.evidence: Hand simulation: the intake share-locks witness W_a and then requests W_b (UUID order). research_reserve_inventory holds W_b FOR UPDATE after mutating SKU B and then requests W_a (f1821b6:33; doc49:67,110 on the FEFO-vs-UUID inversion). This cycle needs no head. The backend that detects the deadlock aborts, which may be the reserve unless the intake's lock_timeout fires first. Items 4 and 6 (7b1e606:17,21) leave the predicate to Samuel and inventory replacement conditional (md:70,138).
findings.fix: Existence predicate: take witnesses FOR SHARE SKIP LOCKED (pick another qualified lot) or NOWAIT (refuse), in UUID order, then recheck allocatability using database time. Quantity predicate: NOWAIT. The intake then never waits on lots, and the conditional inventory family is needed only for a remaining proven incompatibility.

findings.claim: No refusal taxonomy separates definite from unknown commit outcomes. Definite in-transaction refusals would read as 'could not confirm receipt' and leave the client stuck in unknown mode.
findings.evidence: supabase-repository.ts:229-301@25858ad maps only 23505 (conflict), 40001 ('Retry the request'), P0001 details for other flows, and otherwise a generic Error. handler.mjs:199-201,108-111 turns any non-InputError into 503 'could not confirm receipt'. QuickOrderPage.tsx:141 unlocks only on 422 invalid_input or 409 catalog_changed/terms_changed; anything else stays unknown (:165-167). While held, a retry gets 503 feature_disabled (handler:121-122), so the customer stays 'unconfirmed' although nothing was saved. JSON:1279 names no codes. InputError is exported (core.mjs:8).
findings.fix: Define a SQL errcode/detail for each refusal class and map it in the in-scope adapter. held/epoch/stale → 409 catalog_changed; Health/standing/session → 409 terms_changed or 401; payload conflict → 409 idempotency_conflict; 55P03/57014/40P01/40001/transport errors → 503 unknown.

A service_role or transport-level setting would bound every service_role RPC, not only QO. Packet JSON:1276-1288 is silent.
findings.fix: Name the mechanism and its blast radius. Either amend item 13 explicitly to allow lock_timeout in the commit's pinned proconfig (with a transport or role setting bounding the statement), or use a dedicated role or PostgREST setting. Require the intake lock_timeout to be below deadlock_timeout. The values stay Samuel's.
